newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says to become more environment conscious.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says to become more environment conscious.

text.p: Japan's top car maker Toyota Motor Corp on Wednesday pledged to strive harder to offer automobiles which are friendly to the environment.

"From this year, I promise we will commit ourselves even more strongly to environmental issues and we will forge ahead with our 'Eco-Project' (by which the company will offer environmentally friendly products)," Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda told reporters.
"In our company management issues, Toyota has given top priority to conserving the environment. The reduction of car emissions is the responsibility of car makers," Okuda said.

"Toyota will make utmost efforts to try to drastically reduce emissions of carbon dioxide, hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides," said Okuda, speaking at a forum on Toyota's involvement in environmental issues.

In one or two years, Toyota plans to launch a vehicle equipped with a new diesel engine which improves fuel efficiency by 25 percent compared with conventional diesel engines, said Toyota's executive vice president Akihiro Wada.
Wada also said Toyota will introduce a "hybrid" car powered by gasoline and batteries within this year.
The fuel consumption of hybrid cars is half of that of Toyota's popular Corolla model, while emissions are one-tenth.
In June, Toyota said it would build an assembly line for its "hybrid" car in Aichi Prefecture, central Japan.
Toyota has a wide range of innovative emission-reducing engines.
Last Thursday in California, Toyota said it would start marketing its RAV4-EV electric vehicle, with a suggested retail price of $42,000.
In December last year, Toyota started selling ultra-lean burn engine Corona cars in Japan, which consumes 30 percent less fuel and cuts carbon dioxide emissions by 30 percent.
The great advantage of being a large company, with a broad range of vehicle types, is that many different approaches to the problems of the future can be undertaken, Okuda said.
"Toyota should take the lead on environmental conservation by offering various kinds of environmentally friendly technologies and products. It's the mission for Japan's top (car) maker," Okuda said.
In June Toyota said it would start using lead-free wire later this year. The new wire harness would help car makers reduce their use of lead which harms the environment.
Toyota has also been developing cars which used compressed natural gas as fuel, an electric car powered by a fuel cell and produces no toxic emissions.
Toyota has not set a time schedule for commercialising the fuel cell car. Fuel cells were originally developed to power space crafts.
